title: The Peasant and the Devil

full_text:
A crafty peasant had plowed his field until twilight when he saw a mound of glowing embers in the middle of the furrow. Approaching cautiously, he found a black, impish devil sitting upon the coals, grinning maliciously.

"Are you sitting upon hidden treasure?" asked the peasant.

"Indeed I am!" replied the devil. "More gold and silver than you have ever seen in all your days! And it shall be yours on one condition: for two years, you must share the harvest of this field with me. What grows above the ground shall belong to me, and what grows beneath the earth shall belong to you."

The peasant agreed with a hearty handshake. When planting time arrived, the clever peasant sowed turnips and carrots. When autumn came, the devil arrived to collect his share, finding only withered yellow leaves and dry weeds, while the peasant dug up great wagons of plump, juicy roots and sweet turnips!

Furious at being outwitted, the devil cried: "Next year the agreement is reversed! What grows beneath the earth belongs to me, and what grows above the ground belongs to you!"

"Agreed," smiled the peasant. The following spring, the peasant sowed wheat and oats. When harvest season returned, the peasant reaped golden grain and heavy sheaves of wheat, while the furious devil was left to dig up useless hairy roots and stubble from the dirt.

Seeing that he could never outsmart the honest peasant's practical agricultural wisdom, the devil screamed in frustration and plunged deep into the fiery depths, leaving the peasant to unearth the colossal chest of gold and silver in complete peace.
moral: A clever and industrious peasant can easily outsmart the greed of sinister schemers.

quiz.question: What is the central moral lesson taught in "The Peasant and the Devil"?
options: Presence of mind and quiet wisdom triumph over brute strength.
Acting in haste and anger without thinking
Believing rumors and flattery without proof
quiz.hint: Remember the moral lesson of this traditional story.

quiz.question: How do the characters overcome their challenge?
options: Through patience, calm reflection, and wisdom
By shouting loudly and blaming others
By running away from every problem
quiz.hint: Consider the virtues praised in world folklore.

quiz.question: What memorable conclusion does this story teach young readers?
options: Honesty, kindness, and clear thinking lead to peace
